Looking at this problem, I need to determine whether the natural map $f$ between the espace étalé of $\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G}$ (over $X$) and the espace étalé of $\mathcal{G}$ (over $Y$) is continuous.

**Answer: Yes, $f$ is continuous.**

## Proof

**Setup and notation.** Let $\pi: X \to Y$ be continuous and $\mathcal{G}$ a sheaf on $Y$. The inverse image sheaf $\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G}$ is the sheafification of the presheaf
$$P(U) = \varinjlim_{V \supseteq \pi(U),\, V \text{ open in } Y} \mathcal{G}(V), \qquad U \subset X \text{ open.}$$
For each $p \in X$, the stalk satisfies
$$(\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G})_p = \varinjlim_{p \in U} P(U) = \varinjlim_{p \in U}\, \varinjlim_{\pi(U)\subseteq V} \mathcal{G}(V) \cong \varinjlim_{\pi(p)\in V} \mathcal{G}(V) = \mathcal{G}_{\pi(p)},$$
since any pair $(U, V)$ with $p \in U$ and $\pi(U) \subseteq V$ satisfies $\pi(p) \in V$, and conversely any $V \ni \pi(p)$ admits $U$ small enough with $\pi(U) \subseteq V$ (by continuity of $\pi$). The isomorphism $f_p: (\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G})_p \to \mathcal{G}_{\pi(p)}$ sends the class of $(U, V, t)$ (with $p \in U$, $\pi(U) \subseteq V$, $t \in \mathcal{G}(V)$) to the germ $t_{\pi(p)}$.

The map $f: \bigsqcup_{p \in X} (\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G})_p \to \bigsqcup_{q \in Y} \mathcal{G}_q$ is $f(p, \alpha) = (\pi(p),\, f_p(\alpha))$.

**Key construction.** Given a basic open set $B(V, t) = \{(q, t_q) : q \in V\}$ in the espace étalé of $\mathcal{G}$ (with $V \subseteq Y$ open, $t \in \mathcal{G}(V)$), set $U = \pi^{-1}(V)$, which is open in $X$ by continuity of $\pi$. Since $\pi(U) \subseteq V$, the section $t \in \mathcal{G}(V)$ defines an element of $P(U)$ via the colimit, and via the sheafification map $P \to \pi^{-1}\mathcal{G}$ we obtain a section $\tilde{t} \in (\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G})(U)$.

**Claim.** $f^{-1}(B(V,t)) = B(U, \tilde{t}) := \{(p, \tilde{t}_p) : p \in U\}$, which is a basic open set in the espace étalé of $\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G}$.

*Proof of claim.* 

($\supseteq$) If $(p, \tilde{t}_p) \in B(U, \tilde{t})$, then $p \in U = \pi^{-1}(V)$, so $\pi(p) \in V$. By construction of $f_p$, the germ $\tilde{t}_p$ (represented by $(U, V, t)$) maps to $t_{\pi(p)}$, i.e., $f_p(\tilde{t}_p) = t_{\pi(p)}$. Hence $f(p, \tilde{t}_p) = (\pi(p), t_{\pi(p)}) \in B(V,t)$.

($\subseteq$) If $(p, \alpha) \in f^{-1}(B(V,t))$, then $\pi(p) \in V$ (so $p \in U$) and $f_p(\alpha) = t_{\pi(p)}$. Since $f_p$ is an isomorphism, $\alpha = f_p^{-1}(t_{\pi(p)})$. But $f_p(\tilde{t}_p) = t_{\pi(p)}$ gives $\tilde{t}_p = f_p^{-1}(t_{\pi(p)}) = \alpha$. So $(p, \alpha) = (p, \tilde{t}_p) \in B(U, \tilde{t})$. $\square$

**Conclusion.** The preimage of every basic open set in the espace étalé of $\mathcal{G}$ is a basic open set (hence open) in the espace étalé of $\pi^{-1}\mathcal{G}$. Since the basic open sets form a basis for the topology, and preimages commute with unions, the preimage of any open set is open. Therefore $f$ is continuous. $\blacksquare$
